evidence.note: Ten explicit TaskCreate milestones forming a dependency-ordered hierarchy: health/persistence skeleton → parser → functions → dynamic-arrays/spill → recompute/CIRC/iterative → CRUD → analyst surface → goal-seek → collab → SPA. This is genuine decomposition sequenced by dependency, well above a flat to-do list.
TaskUpdate in_progress/completed transitions per milestone show live state tracking of the milestone plan across the build.

After the smoke suite passed, a NEW milestone was created targeting hidden-grader edge cases (WS since_seq backfill, last-write-wins, iterative calc) — the plan is revisited/extended as scope understanding deepens, not a static checklist.
Milestone done-checks are tied to runnable evidence: dev_tests runs plus 1k/5k/100k perf benchmarks and cycle/persistence probes, with fixes (201-215) when perf milestones failed their checks.

Weakness vs anchor 8: nearly all modules were batch-written (46-97) and milestones marked completed on code-written; the live server/health round-trip was not verified until step 99-100, AFTER breadth was already built rather than green-before-breadth.

reasoning: The agent produced an explicit, dependency-ordered milestone hierarchy (34-43) with per-milestone state tracking (44-105), done-checks tied to runnable tests and benchmarks (107-230), and re-planned mid-flight by adding an edge-case milestone (148) — clearly beyond anchor 5's rough checkpoints. It falls short of a clean 8/10 because it did not achieve the anchor's defining behavior of getting a live server + persistence + contract-correct core round-trip green before building breadth: modules were batch-written and marked complete on code-written, with verification batched afterward. That places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, near the top of that band due to the dependency sequencing and genuine re-planning.
